Thanks for taking our call last week. Our engineering team has a few follow-ups before we proceed with an eval: primarily, how Redwood charges for the conversational endpoints. We currently use two patterns and want to map them to your rate card:

- Chat-style conversational workloads (back-and-forth UI) — we've been trying both the new Responses endpoint and the legacy completions-based chat wrapper.
- Short single-turn prompts (tooling and notifications) — generally small input, small output.

Specifically: can you confirm how tokens/units are counted for Chat Completions vs Responses vs the legacy completions endpoint? Our finance team also asked for a baseline hosted rate and any volume discount schedule you can share.

I've attached a short usage snapshot (estimated monthly tokens + sample requests) to help you size this. Looking to get a written mapping we can present internally.

NeonRetail

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Endpoint unit mapping and discount inquiry

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the note and the attachment. Short answer up front: the three endpoint flavors are priced differently and map to billing units in slightly different ways. I've attached our current hosted rate card (Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_v3.pdf) and a SOC2 summary you can forward to procurement.

High-level mapping (summary):
- Chat Completions (conversational API): billed per input + output tokens. This is the most common pattern for interactive UIs; system + user + assistant tokens all count toward the token total for the request.
- Responses (new unified responses endpoint): billed by response units (we surface this as output-token-weighted units). In practice Responses charges are dominated by the model output size — for streaming use-cases it can be more cost-efficient because you only pay for produced tokens and we optimize network/compute paths.
- Legacy completions (text-completion endpoints): billed per token too, but priced under legacy SKUs which are slightly higher per-token due to older routing and compatibility layers.

Key practical notes:
- Prefix/KV cache savings: for long conversations you may see effective cost savings with Chat Completions when prefix tokens are cached; Responses optimizations can reduce compute for many single-turn calls.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming output doesn't change the token accounting, but can change latency profiles and effective throughput (affects FTE cost to your engineers, not our units).

I've looped in Lauren (pricing/GT M) and Diego (solution engineering) to propose a short discount/commit framework once we see confirmed monthly volumes. Can we hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to run through the usage snapshot?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for sending the estimate and thanks Sean for the context. For procurement clarity, here are the standard headline options we typically offer for Hosted API (we can tailor):

- Standard (no commitment): list rate as in the attached PDF.
- Committed monthly spend tiers: 10% discount at $20k/mo commit, 15% at $50k/mo, 20% at $120k/mo.
- Enterprise volume + SLA: custom pricing (20%+) for 12–24mo contracts with reserved capacity and priority support.

Note on billing units and mapping: when customers migrate from legacy completions to Responses we typically run a 30–60 day calibration where we normalize billing to a common token baseline so you can compare spend. We documented the expected per-request conversions in the attached rate-diff-sheet.xlsx — it includes a sample reconciliation:

- Example: a 300-token input + 900-token output conversation
   * Chat Completions: charged on 1,200 tokens at hosted chat rate.
   * Responses: charged primarily on the 900 output tokens converted to response units (we show per-model multipliers in the sheet).
   * Legacy completions: charged on 1,200 tokens at legacy SKU price (higher unit price).

Action items: please confirm expected monthly committed spend band (ballpark) and whether you need a fixed per-token mapping period to evaluate migration impact. I'm happy to draft a short mutual action plan after we have that.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop

lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Hi Olivia —

Per your procurement ask, here is a concise, procurement-friendly mapping and an approximate per-1k-token delta between Responses and legacy completions for the models we recommend for NeonRetail (practical, not perfectly precise):

Table (text):
- Chat Completions (conversational API) -> counts: input + output tokens (system + user + assistant). Typical pricing impact: mid-range per-token. Notes: good for long-form chat with caching benefits.
- Responses (unified responses endpoint) -> counts: primarily output-weighted response units (output tokens are the dominant factor). Typical pricing impact: ~10–25% lower per-1k-output-token compared to legacy completions for the same model family because of routing and compute optimizations.
- Legacy completions -> counts: input + output tokens. Typical pricing impact: baseline legacy SKU price; generally 15–30% higher per-1k-token than Responses depending on model and sequence length.

Approx per-1k-token delta (illustrative):
- Responses vs Legacy Completions: Responses ~ $0.80–$1.10 per 1k-output-tokens; Legacy Completions ~ $1.00–$1.40 per 1k-output-tokens. (Range depends on model family: smaller models toward the low end, largest models toward the high end.)
- Chat Completions effective cost depends on conversation length due to caching. Example above (1.2k tokens total) typically maps to legacy-completions price if you remain on legacy SKUs; moving to Responses usually reduces cost by ~12% on that sample.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you can confirm a target committed spend band (a ballpark is fine: e.g., $10–30k/mo or $50–100k/mo), we'll send a one-page MPP (mutual plan + pricing) with exact tiered discounts and proposed trial normalization period.
2) Diego can run a short ingestion of a week of telemetry against Responses to produce an expected monthly spend delta for your exact traffic shape.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk procurement through the numbers.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
